newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Spanish "mobile phone" hijacker on trial in Geneva.
newsitem.headline: Spanish "mobile phone" hijacker on trial in Geneva.

text.p: A Spaniard accused of threatening to blow up a French airliner with a fake "detonator" made from a mobile phone went on trial in Geneva on Thursday facing life imprisonment.

The Swiss news agency ATS said the industrial designer from Palma de Mallorca in Spain, who briefly hijacked the Air Inter Airbus plane in September 1995 and forced it to land at Geneva's Cointrin airport, could escape a life sentence at the two-day trial if psychiatric experts concluded he was mentally unstable.

The hijacker, identified by Spanish state radio as Carlos Santolaya, had threatened to blow up the plane during a flight from Palma de Mallorca to Paris in protest at France's plans to resume nuclear testing in the South Pacific.

The Spaniard surrendered after releasing the 298 passengers on board when the plane landed. What he claimed to be a remote-control detonator turned out to be a mobile telephone with batteries taped to it.
ATS said two psychiatric experts remained divided over the hijacker's mental health, with one concluding he was responsible for his acts and the other declaring he was unbalanced.
